requirements.text: All questions to the bank must be sent in writing through the bank's tender portal.
Suppliers shall not contact other bank employees about this competition during the process.
The tender must be written in English.
The tender must be submitted through the tender portal before the deadline (22 January 2027, 12:00 CET). Late tenders will be rejected.
The tender shall be signed by a person authorised to bind the supplier.
The tender must be valid for six months after the tender deadline.
The solution description (Appendix B) should not exceed 60 pages. Marketing material will not be evaluated.

Any reservations or deviations from the requirements or draft contract must be stated clearly in a separate list. Unlisted reservations are disregarded; significant reservations may lead to rejection.
Answer each requirement in Appendix A as met, partly met or not met, and describe how. Requirements without an ID must also be answered, referencing the section number.
The supplier shall hold a valid ISO/IEC 27001 certification covering the services offered.
Document at least two reference customers among banks in the Nordics or EU/EEA where comparable account or data solutions were delivered within the last five years.
The supplier shall have a credit rating or financial statements showing sufficient financial capacity for a contract of this size.
Confirm that the supplier can provide the information needed for the bank's DORA register of information, including subcontractors supporting critical functions.
Support deposit accounts for retail and business customers, including current accounts, savings accounts and fixed-term deposits.
Calculate interest and fees according to the bank's product rules, including tiered interest rates.
The bank should be able to configure and launch a new account product without changes to program code.
Support joint accounts and accounts with several authorised users, with different rights per user.
The solution should support sub-accounts or "savings pots" linked to a main account.
Handle account opening, changes and closure, including a full history of all changes.
Support blocking of accounts and amounts, for example for fraud cases or legal seizure.
Balances and transactions must be updated in real time, so the mobile app, online bank and adviser tools show the same information within two seconds of a booking.
The solution should publish account events (e.g. booking made, balance changed, account blocked) as event streams that other systems can subscribe to.
During transition the solution must run in parallel with the current core system, with daily reconciliation of balances between old and new solution.
Describe how the solution handles peak loads, such as salary days and the days before Christmas.
All account services shall be available through documented REST APIs, with an OpenAPI specification.
Support third-party access to account information and payment initiation based on customer consent, in line with PSD2 and Berlin Group NextGenPSD2.
The solution should be prepared for PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation. Describe your plan.
The solution should offer a developer portal with a test environment (sandbox) for partners.
Log all API calls with time, caller and consent reference, and keep the logs for at least five years.
The solution should support APIs for SME accounting platforms so business customers can get account data directly into their accounting system.
Provide a common data model for customers, accounts, products and transactions, documented and available to the bank.
The bank should be able to define data products (e.g. "customer engagement", "deposit flows") with a named owner, definition and quality rules.
Measure and report data quality (completeness, accuracy, timeliness) for the data products.
The solution should keep the full data lineage from source system to report.
The bank shall be able to extract all its data in an open, documented format at any time and at the end of the contract.
The data platform should let analysts use their own tools (SQL, Python) on governed data, without copying data to unmanaged spreadsheets.
Deliver the account and transaction data needed for regulatory reporting to Finanstilsynet, Norges Bank and Statistics Norway, with documented calculation rules.
The solution should support reconciliation between reporting data and the general ledger, with automatic alerts on differences.
Describe how changes in reporting requirements are handled and who is responsible for updating the solution.
Describe AI functions in the solution, or planned in the roadmap, that can help advisers or improve data quality.
For every AI function, describe what data is used, how results can be explained, and where a person must review or approve the result.
AI functions shall not make automated decisions about customers without human review, unless the bank has explicitly approved it.
Customer data shall not be used to train AI models outside the bank's own environment without the bank's written consent.
Describe how the solution supports the bank's obligations under the EU AI Act.
Customer data shall be stored and processed within the EU/EEA, including backups and support access.
All data shall be encrypted in transit and at rest.
Access controlled with role-based access and multi-factor authentication for all administrative users.
Notify the bank of serious ICT incidents without undue delay and no later than four hours after detection.
Take part in the bank's resilience testing, including threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) when required by the authorities.
Have a documented exit plan allowing the bank to move the service to another supplier or back in-house.
The supplier should provide a recent independent assurance report (ISAE 3402 type 2 or equivalent) each year.
Customer-facing services shall be available 99.95 % of the time per month, measured outside agreed maintenance windows.
Planned maintenance must be done at night (01:00–05:00) and announced at least 14 days in advance.
Offer support in English and Norwegian, 24/7 for critical incidents.
The solution should support recovery after a serious incident with an RTO of max 4 hours and an RPO of max 5 minutes.
The supplier should report monthly on availability, incidents, capacity and service requests.
Propose a phased delivery plan (no "big bang") where each phase gives value to customers or the bank and can be taken into use on its own.
The plan should start with the area where the supplier believes value is highest and risk lowest, and explain why.
Describe the migration approach for accounts and history, including test migrations, reconciliation and fallback if a migration step fails.
Describe which roles and how much capacity the bank's IT team (about 35 people) must provide in each phase.
Name the key persons for delivery (at least project manager and solution architect) and describe their relevant experience.
Give the price in the price form (Appendix C), in NOK excluding VAT, covering all costs needed to deliver the requirements.
The supplier should offer a price model where part of the payment is linked to delivery of agreed milestones.
The supplier shall accept the bank's right to audit, as required by Finanstilsynet's outsourcing rules.

key_dates.event: Minimum tender validity: six months after the tender deadline

clarification_questions.question: Section 2.4 says the solution description 'should not exceed 60 pages', but Appendix B is labelled 'max 60 pages'. Is the limit mandatory or guidance? Do CVs, references, the Appendix A response form and other attachments count towards it?
Requirements in running text use 'must' (real-time updates, parallel running, maintenance window) alongside 'should'. Can the bank confirm that 'must' and 'shall' are equivalent and mandatory?
How is the two-second update time measured (end-to-end from booking to display in the channels, or only to the platform's output)? At what percentile, and under what load?

SEC-01 requires support access from within the EU/EEA, while 5.8 requires 24/7 support for critical incidents. Is follow-the-sun support from outside the EU/EEA excluded entirely, or allowed without access to customer data?
Which services count as 'customer-facing' for the 99.95 % availability requirement? Are outages caused by the bank's own channels or third parties excluded?

What definition of a 'serious ICT incident' applies (e.g. the DORA major-incident classification)? Does the four-hour clock start at detection by the supplier or when the supplier classifies the incident?

Must the ISO/IEC 27001 certificate be valid at the tender deadline, or is a certification in progress acceptable? Does it also have to cover critical subcontractors? What minimum level of financial capacity (rating or equity ratio) does the bank require?

Which specific reports to Finanstilsynet, Norges Bank and Statistics Norway must the platform provide data for? Is the supplier expected to produce the reports themselves, or only the underlying data?
The bank may award without negotiation. Should the first tender therefore be a best-and-final offer? Can reservations and prices be revised during negotiations?
Does the six-year total cost in the price form include the extension options (2 + 2 years)? How will the options be priced and evaluated?

Please share the Annual Report extract, the strategy note, the AI policy (available on request) and Appendices A–D, in particular the Appendix A response template and the draft contract, so that reservations can be assessed.
